summary.text: Christine Drazan, a Republican Oregon state senator, lost the November 3, 2026 election for Governor of Oregon to Tina Kotek, who also defeated her in 2022.
She served in the Oregon House from 2019 to 2022, including as Minority Leader, and returned as Minority Leader in 2025 before being appointed to the Senate.

paragraphs.text: Drazan was born in Klamath Falls and raised in Southern Oregon, and she graduated from George Fox University with a bachelor's degree in communications.
In the 1990s she worked for House Speaker Mark Simmons, in a role Wikipedia describes as communications director and Ballotpedia as chief of staff.
She was later political coordinator for the Oregon Restaurant and Lodging Association from 2006 to 2011 and executive director of the Cultural Advocacy Coalition from 2011 to 2018.
Drazan was elected to the Oregon House in 2018, representing District 39, and served as House Republican leader from 2019 to 2021.
She was the Republican nominee for governor in 2022 and lost to Tina Kotek.
After winning the 2024 election for House District 51, she returned as Minority Leader in 2025.
In October 2025 county commissioners appointed her to Oregon Senate District 26 to fill the vacancy left by Daniel Bonham, and she announced her 2026 campaign for governor days later.
Ballotpedia listed her on the November ballot as both a Republican and a Libertarian Party candidate.
During the campaign, she emphasized cutting taxes, loosening building and land-use rules, and steering people experiencing homelessness into treatment.
She received 43.7% of the vote to Tina Kotek's 53.3%, according to unofficial results reported by NBC News.
